paraphrase: Things do not arise from themselves, because their arising would be pointless and because of the fault of absurd consequence: for things already existing in their own being there is no purpose in arising again, and if what exists were to arise, it would never cease arising.

original.text: na svata utpadyante bhāvāḥ, tadutpādavaiyarthyāt, atiprasaṅgadoṣācca | na hi svātmanā vidyamānānāṃ padārthānāṃ punarutpāde prayojanamasti | atha sannapi jāyeta, na kadācinna jāyeta iti ||
